title: graphty recipe member, version 1
description: A journal of analysis commands -- filters, algorithm runs and a layout -- replayed on any graph whose import has the columns it names (recipe.md). Normative for what a writer produces. The members of each known command, and of its scope, are closed: a reader skips a command with a member it does not know, and every command after it (recipe.md, 'Replaying'). The parts of a run's style are open: a reader drops a part it does not know. op is an open list: a command of a later op is valid, and a reader stops the replay there. Two-segment ops in the graph, algo, layout, column, style and data families are graphty-element's; others have three or more segments and start with a reverse-domain name. A commands entry that is not an object or has no op stops the replay as an unknown op does.

id.description: The recipe's identity across all its versions. A reverse-domain name (org.example.hub-genes) or an https: URL is recommended, so two authors do not collide. Ids starting graphty. or graphty:, and ids holding graphty.app followed by /, :, . or the end, in any case, are reserved for the recipes graphty-element ships, so no spelling of a graphty.app URL gets through.

recipeVersion.description: One version of the recipe, as a SemVer 2.0.0 version.

namespace.description: The namespace this recipe's run ids prefer when it is applied (recipe.md, 'Run ids and namespaces'). Letters, digits and single underscores, so a namespaced run id needs no quoting in a path.

directed.description: The direction of the graph the recipe was recorded on. A replay on a graph of the other direction is reported (recipe.md, 'Binding to a new graph' rule 5).

parallelEdges.description: Whether the graph the recipe was recorded on held more than one edge between a pair of nodes. false makes a replay on a graph that does hold them report it before anything runs (recipe.md, 'Binding to a new graph' rule 5).

table.description: For data read from a table (CSV): how it is read. Defaults for a table imported for this recipe through its application's import() or as the file's own data member; the caller's options win, and the endpoint columns, delimiter and variant are used only when the file's first line holds the reading's endpoint columns. A list is tried in order and the first reading that passes is used (recipe.md, 'Table data'). Ignored for formats that mark endpoints themselves.

generator.description: The release that recorded the recipe. recipes.record() writes it; a replay on another release is reported (recipe.md, 'Same data, same results').

command.description: Dispatched on op, so a validator reports only the errors of the command kind named.

tableColumn.description: A column name, looked up as a plain name, never evaluated.

delimiter.description: The character that separates columns; the importer's own detection when absent.

variant.description: The CSV shape, as graphty-element's catalogue names it (edge-list, node-list, ...). A reading whose variant is neo4j passes its header test when the first line holds :START_ID and :END_ID, or :ID, and then reads the file as that variant, whose header types its own structure (recipe.md, 'Table data' rule 3).

repeatedEdges.description: What a second edge between the same two nodes becomes. sum, min and max combine one column, the edge weight or the one combineColumn names; every other column of a merged edge is its first row's (its last row's for last).

combineColumn.description: The column sum, min and max combine, kept under its own name; the edge weight when absent.

columns.description: Renames for this tool's headers: the recipe's column name to the header that holds it ({"volume": "amount"}). The header test requires every header named here; the renames apply only when this reading passes it, before the weight is found, and the recipe's commands and the file's styles then bind to the recipe's names. For a neo4j reading, a header is named without its type suffix (recipe.md, 'Table data' rule 1).

nodeColumns.description: The same, for this tool's node table only: only a node table is tested for these headers.

edgeColumns.description: The same, for this tool's edge table only: only an edge table is tested for these headers.

filterWhileReading.description: Apply the recipe's leading edge filters to each row while the table is read even when rows are merged: a pair is kept when any of its rows passes. Without it, a table whose rows are merged is read whole and filtered after import (recipe.md, 'Table data' rule 4). Default false.

tableReading.description: One way of reading a table: the import option names of container.md, 'Import options' -- the columns holding an edge's two ends and a node's id, the delimiter, the CSV shape, what repeated rows become and the column they combine -- plus filterWhileReading and the renames columns, nodeColumns and edgeColumns. Its members follow the import options, which grow within version 1; a reader tries the readings in order up to the first one holding a member it does not know, and refuses the import there when none before it passed (recipe.md, 'Table data' rule 7).

predicate.description: A predicate in graphty-element's expression language (style.md, 'Expressions') over the table 'on' names: columns as data.<column> or by their bare name (confidence >= 0.4), earlier results as results.<as>.<field>; numbers, true, false and null may be written bare. Reads columns only: the structural paths of style.md, 'Paths' rule 4 are refused.

on.description: nodes (the default): keep the matched nodes and the edges between them. edges: keep the matched edges; every node stays unless dropIsolated.

dropIsolated.description: Also drop every node left with no edge once this filter's rule has applied, including one that had none before. Default false.

graphFilter.description: Narrows the graph every later command of the recipe sees, and shows it as the session's filter (recipe.md, 'Commands' rule 13).

as.description: The run's name in this recipe. Unique within the recipe; letters, digits and single underscores, never two underscores in a row, which separate a namespace from a name, so a path naming the run needs no quoting. Its meaning never changes between recipe versions.

params.description: Option values by the option names graphty-element's catalogue publishes for the algorithm or layout. An option of type attribute or partition may instead name an earlier run's result as {"result": "<as>.<field>"} (recipe.md, 'Commands' rule 4). The algorithm's own seed option is not given here: seed is (a command that gives it is skipped).

on.description: Which table the predicate is evaluated on. nodes (the default): the run sees the matched nodes and the edges between them. edges: the run sees every node and only the matched edges.

description.description: Why this command is in the recipe. Shown to people; never sent to the algorithm.

algorithm.description: An algorithm key from graphty-element's catalogue, or one a plugin registered.

seed.description: The run's seed. Its maximum is the smallest seed range among graphty-element's algorithms. Absent: the algorithm's published default seed, or one drawn at run time when it has none (recipe.md, 'Commands' rule 7).

recordedCapSeconds.description: Advisory: the per-command cost cap the run was recorded under, when it was above the default. A replay never raises its cap from it; the report quotes it beside E_CAP_EXCEEDED so the person replaying knows what to pass (recipe.md, 'Running' rule 2).

recordedPrecision.description: Advisory: the precision the run was recorded in, from its caveats and spelled as they spell it (f32 on a WebGPU accelerator, f64 on the CPU). A replay in the other precision is reported (W_PRECISION_DIFFERS); it never asks for a precision.

style.description: What the run paints when it completes: the run's RunStyle, as graphty-element's run option of the same name. true, the colouring its result suggests; false, nothing; the object form, only the parts it names. Absent, it paints unless a style member of the same file reads this run's results. The parts of the object form grow within version 1: a reader drops a part it does not know and paints the rest (recipe.md, 'Replaying' rule 3).

id.description: A layout id from graphty-element's catalogue, or one a plugin registered.

engine.description: The engine that draws the layout; the catalogue's default engine for id when absent.

options.description: The engine's options, by the names the catalogue publishes, the seed among them.

narrows.description: The author's statement that this command changes nothing a later command sees. A reader that does not know the op then skips only it and the commands that read its as, instead of every later command (recipe.md, 'Replaying' rule 4). Every op a release adds admits this member, and a reader that knows the op ignores it.

laterCommand.description: A command a later release adds. An op of two segments whose first is graph, algo, layout, column, style or data is graphty-element's; anyone else's op has three or more segments and starts with a reverse-domain name (org.example.motif-census). Lower case, so algo.Run, algorun and acme.census are refused here; a misspelling in the right form (algo.rnu) is caught only by a reader. A version 1 reader skips it and every later command (E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND, then E_DEPENDENCY_SKIPPED), unless it says narrows: false. A later command that names its result does so in as, as algo.run does.
